To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the probability of user and graph isolation can be reduced by using age-biased strategies in unstructured P2Ps, and (2) this reduction is significant for heavy-tailed distributions and increases monotonically as the size and age of the system grows.
the resilience of unstructured P 2 P systems is improved by age-biased strategies that select neighbors based on their age, which in turn improves the performance of the network.

the probability of node isolation in unstructured P2Ps with heavy-tailed lifetimes and arbitrary selection of neighbors converges to zero when the average age of the system and the number of users tend to infinity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the resilience of unstructured P 2 P systems to user isolation and graph fragmentation.
the resilience of unstructured P 2P networks to node failures.
improving the robustness of large-scale P2P systems by increasing the resilience of user neighborhoods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the age-biased strategies are more resilient and more robust to the user-lifetime distributions than the uniform strategy.

, in unstructured P2Ps, the age of users is the most critical parameter to consider in order to improve resilience, and that random walks in age-proportional graph are the best strategy to achieve this goal.
age-biased node-selection policies significantly increase the resilience of unstructured P 2 P systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the age-biased strategies are more robust than the uniform selection in the face of heavy-tailed lifetimes and that the random walk strategy is the most resilient of the two.
, in order to achieve a high level of resilience against user churn, a P2P system needs to employ age-biased algorithms for selecting neighbors.
, in unstructured P2Ps, the resilience of the system is not limited by the number of peers, but by their age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age of users is a crucial factor to consider when designing resilient P2P systems.

age-based selection of neighbors is a simple and effective strategy that improves the robustness of unstructured PVR systems, even in the absence of any additional mechanism to maintain network connectivity.
the resilience of unstructured P 2P networks is much greater than previous analytical studies indicate.
